periods.analysis: Average pothole repair time opened the series at 3.1 days, comfortably green against the <=5-day target. This is peak paving weather, so the number is helped by hot-mix availability from North Bay Asphalt and two full street maintenance crews running the Route 4 coastal loop and the inland arterial loop. We also started tagging repeat defects in Cityworks against pavement segments such as HV-PV-1172 on Harbor Boulevard instead of treating every hole like a new surprise. That is the right engineering habit: measure the asset, then send the crew.
periods.recommendations: Keep the two-loop dispatch model through the fall shoulder season and preserve the 7:00 a.m. hot-mix pickup slot with North Bay Asphalt. Use the Cityworks repeat-defect tags to build a top-25 segment list for the FY2025 resurfacing package, not just for daily patching. I want a short weekly exception report on any repair exceeding 5 days so we defend the green result with evidence, not luck.

periods.analysis: Repair time moved from 3.1 days to 3.9 days, a 0.8-day increase, but it remains green and still 1.1 days inside the <=5-day target. The rise is consistent with wetter pavement, shorter daylight, and crew time diverted to inlet clearing on the Bayview and Seacliff routes. We also saw more utility-cut edge failures after franchise work on Maple Avenue, especially around pavement segment HV-PV-2046. The pipes and wires do not care about our quarterly chart, but the street surface still has to be closed out cleanly.
periods.recommendations: Hold the green by pairing one pothole truck with the drainage crew on rain days so failed pavement around inlets is patched on the same pass. Require the franchise utility vendors on Maple Avenue and East Marina Drive to submit 48-hour cut-restoration photos before we accept the permit closeout. Keep a small cold-mix reserve at Yard 2 for weekend calls when the plant is down.

periods.analysis: The measure rose again from 3.9 days to 4.2 days, a 0.3-day increase, but stayed green under the <=5-day standard. That is a winter number, not a failure number: freeze-thaw opened seams on older collector streets, and cold-mix patches are slower and less durable than hot mix. Crew 12 logged the heaviest call volume on school access streets near West Harbor Elementary and along the Transit Route 7 corridor. The trend is worth watching, but the service level is still where a city with our traffic load should be.
periods.recommendations: Continue prioritizing school frontage, transit corridors, and bike-lane hazards first in the dispatch queue, with routine local streets next. Convert the worst winter repeat locations, including HV-PV-1172 and HV-PV-2046, into mill-and-overlay candidates before the summer bid package closes. Keep tracking repair age by material type so we know exactly how much cold mix is costing us in repeat visits.

periods.analysis: Repair time improved from 4.2 days to 3.8 days, a 0.4-day decrease, and remains green. Hot-mix season returned, and the April 'Patch to Pave' push let crews close older tickets while the contractor handled curb-ramp punch work nearby. We also added a half-day Friday sweep on the waterfront route after resident reports from the 311 mobile app clustered around Pier Street and Ocean Park Drive. That operational change shows up in the number; it is not complicated, just disciplined routing.
periods.recommendations: Make the Friday waterfront sweep permanent through September and assign it a fixed truck, roller, and two-person crew so it does not get borrowed into other work. Extend the 311 cluster review to the North Ridge growth area, where subdivision traffic is starting to beat up collector approaches. Carry the 3.8-day result into the budget narrative as evidence that small crew-hour adjustments can avoid larger pavement deterioration.

periods.analysis: Repair time dropped from 3.8 days to 3 days, a 0.8-day improvement, the best result in this series and well inside the <=5-day target. Summer conditions helped, but the bigger factor was batching work by pavement management zone instead of chasing single tickets across town. Crews closed 312 tickets under the 'Zone 3 Blitz' covering Harbor Boulevard, Keelson Drive, and the civic campus approaches. When the route is tight and the material is hot, the asphalt behaves about as well as asphalt is going to behave.
periods.recommendations: Keep zone batching as the default summer operating model and publish the two-week zone map internally so Traffic, Parks, and Utilities do not schedule conflicting lane work. Use the 3-day performance level to test a same-week closure goal for arterials only, without promising it citywide yet. Lock in 2026 hot-mix pricing early with escalation language, because this result depends on reliable material supply.

periods.analysis: The measure moved from 3 days to 3.8 days, a 0.8-day increase, but it remains green and better than the same winter shoulder period last year. The increase is expected with leaf season, rain, and more crew hours assigned to storm response on the low-lying Shoreline Drive basin. We also saw patch demand rise around new multifamily frontage permits on 9th Street where heavy trucks are loading pavement edges before final wearing course. The number is still sound, but growth is putting weight on the street network one axle at a time.
periods.recommendations: Maintain one protected pothole response crew during storm operations so drainage calls do not consume all pavement capacity. Add permit condition checks on 9th Street and similar frontage projects, including temporary steel plates, edge protection, and final trench restoration dates. Carry forward the zone map, but add a rain-triggered reserve list of indoor fleet and sign work so crews can pivot without losing dispatch discipline.

periods.analysis: Repair time increased from 3.8 days to 4.4 days, a 0.6-day increase, still green but now only 0.6 days below the <=5-day target. This quarter had the usual winter damage plus two atmospheric river weeks that kept patches wet and pushed crews into barricade and sinkhole standby. The Harborview Avenue detour for the water-main work near asset WM-16-044 also shifted more traffic onto older pavement on Cedar and Lark, and the pavement showed it. This is managed, not comfortable; the street system is telling us where the underground work is surfacing at grade.
periods.recommendations: Until Pipeline Renewal work around WM-16-044 is restored, inspect Cedar and Lark twice weekly and pre-stage mix at Yard 1 after major rain events. Keep pothole repair tickets tied to nearby utility assets in Cityworks so we can separate ordinary pavement failures from detour and trench-restoration impacts. Do not cut the spring patching overtime line; the 4.4-day result is green, but it is close enough to the rail to justify the spend.

periods.analysis: Repair time improved from 4.4 days to 3.6 days, a 0.8-day decrease, returning the measure to a stronger green position. Dry weather helped, and so did reopening the Harborview Avenue lanes after the first Pipeline Renewal restoration panels were accepted. Crew 14 used a rolling closure plan on Cedar, Lark, and South Marina that let them finish patches without repeated setup and teardown. That is the practical payoff from coordinating streets and utilities: fewer cones, fewer repeat trips, and a better number in days.
periods.recommendations: Keep the rolling closure template for all corridors affected by Pipeline Renewal and require a joint streets-utilities restoration walk before lanes reopen. Extend the stronger 3.6-day practice by reserving two mornings per week for arterial pothole tickets before crews move to local streets. Use Q1-to-Q2 improvement as the evidence package for retaining the additional patch trailer and infrared heater in the next capital equipment request.

periods.analysis: Illustrative September import: average pothole repair time was 4.1 days, up from 3.6 days but still within the five-day target. The earlier streets-and-utilities rolling closure approach remains useful where restoration work overlaps repairs.
periods.recommendations: Keep joint restoration walks and monitor whether repair tickets near utility work are taking longer than other tickets.
